cards.prompt: 이 동네에는 가족들이 많이 살고 있어서 ___가 많아요
cards.translation: There are a lot of families living in this neighborhood, so there are a lot of apartments
cards.explanation: Konglish consists of Korean words borrowed or adapted from English and used with Korean pronunciation and meaning. In this sentence, the blank expresses the idea shown in the translation: “There are a lot of families living in this neighborhood, so there are a lot of apartments”. Use these familiar-looking words carefully: their Korean meaning, pronunciation and usage may differ from English. There is no single grammar rule. Learn each Konglish item as Korean vocabulary and follow the source examples for spelling and collocation.

lessons.title: Because with ~기에 and ~길래
lessons.explanation: Original practice for the HTSK Lesson 136 focus. Use the official Unit 6 lesson for the full explanation.

cards.translation: Beef was on sale at the supermarket, so I bought a lot of it
cards.explanation: ~기에 and ~길래 can give a reason, with different perspectives and discourse nuances. In this sentence, the blank expresses the idea shown in the translation: “Beef was on sale at the supermarket, so I bought a lot of it”. Use them when explaining a basis or reason, especially when the speaker's discovery or situation motivates the following statement. Attach ~기에 or ~길래 to the first clause using the forms in HTSK; the second clause gives the consequence or response.

lessons.title: Necessity with ~아/어야
lessons.explanation: Original practice for the HTSK Lesson 137 focus. Use the official Unit 6 lesson for the full explanation.

cards.translation: Kimchi must be made at home/with one’s own hands for it to be delicious
cards.explanation: ~아/어야 can express necessity or a condition without the full 하다 expression. In this sentence, the blank expresses the idea shown in the translation: “Kimchi must be made at home/with one’s own hands for it to be delicious”. Use it in constructions where the required condition or action is followed by a result, command or conclusion. Attach ~아야 after a ㅏ/ㅗ stem and ~어야 after other vowels; 하다 becomes 해야, then add the following clause or predicate.

lessons.title: As a role with ~(으)로서
lessons.explanation: Original practice for the HTSK Lesson 140 focus. Use the official Unit 6 lesson for the full explanation.

cards.prompt: ___ 가족을 책임져야 하기 때문에 어깨가 무겁다

cards.explanation: ~(으)로서 means as a role, capacity or position. In this sentence, the blank expresses the idea shown in the translation: “There is a lot of burden on the breadwinner because he/she is responsible for the family”. Use it to identify the role from which someone acts or is evaluated. Attach ~로서 after a vowel and ~으로서 after a consonant; place it after the noun naming the role.

lessons.title: Lesson 142: ~ㄴ/는다니 – Responding in Surprise or Displeasure
lessons.explanation: Original practice for the HTSK Lesson 142 focus. Use the official Unit 6 lesson for the full explanation.

cards.translation: You’re going now? You just got here! Why are you leaving so early?
cards.explanation: HTSK uses ~ㄴ/는다니, ~다니 and related forms to react to information with surprise, displeasure or astonishment. The speaker responds to something just said and adds an emotional attitude. In this sentence, the blank expresses the idea shown in the translation: “You’re going now? You just got here! Why are you leaving so early?”. Use this ending as a short conversational reaction when the previous statement is surprising, unbelievable or displeasing. The exact feeling comes from the context and intonation. Use the plain form followed by 니: 가다 → 간다니, 먹다 → 먹는다니, 먹었다 → 먹었다니, 행복하다 → 행복하다니. With nouns use ~(이)라니; replace 고 in quoted suggestions, questions or commands with 니: 가자니, 가느냐니, 가라니.

lessons.title: Guessing/refuting with ~ㄹ/을걸요
lessons.explanation: Original practice for the HTSK Lesson 143 focus. Use the official Unit 6 lesson for the full explanation.

cards.translation: There probably isn’t anybody there yet

lessons.title: ~지 뭐: resignation and acceptance
lessons.explanation: Original practice for the HTSK Lesson 144 focus. Use the official Unit 6 lesson for the full explanation.

cards.translation: Well, there’s nothing I can do. They say there are no beds, so I guess I’m bringing a sleeping bag.
cards.explanation: ~지 뭐 expresses resignation or acceptance that the outcome cannot be changed, roughly I guess so or then I will. In this sentence, the blank expresses the idea shown in the translation: “Well, there’s nothing I can do. They say there are no beds, so I guess I’m bringing a sleeping bag.”. Use it when the speaker stops worrying about the result and accepts a practical next step. Attach ~지 뭐 to the relevant conjugated predicate; the tone and context carry the resigned attitude described by HTSK.

cards.prompt: ___ 사람들 장 속에 사는 세균을 말한다

lessons.title: Because of being busy with ~느라고
lessons.explanation: Original practice for the HTSK Lesson 146 focus. Use the official Unit 6 lesson for the full explanation.

cards.prompt: 밤길에 ___ 길을 건너는 고양이를 보지 못했다
cards.translation: I didn’t see the cat crossing the street because I was driving at night
cards.explanation: ~느라고 gives a reason based on being occupied with one action, usually with a negative or inconvenient result. In this sentence, the blank expresses the idea shown in the translation: “I didn’t see the cat crossing the street because I was driving at night”. Use it when one activity prevents, delays or causes difficulty for another action. Attach ~느라고 to a verb stem; the subject and tense restrictions and the negative-result nuance are important in HTSK.
